rules.text: block_optimize requires block_size in {2,3,4} AND 4 <= max_gates <= 200. Calls with max_gates=40/60 but block_size outside {2,3,4}, or max_gates<4 or >200, raise ToolError and invalidate the whole run. Validate both bounds before calling.

Build candidates as a flat list via repeated .append(...), then call tools.best(candidates) once with that list, not tools.best(x, y, z) with loose args mixed with tools.best(list). Keep call shape consistent to avoid parse/signature errors.

Diff-style replies must contain the literal SEARCH block text copied exactly (verbatim whitespace/newlines) from the parent program exactly once; paraphrasing or re-indenting the SEARCH snippet causes 'unparseable response' rejection.

tools.best accepts EITHER a single list arg OR multiple loose args, both consistently, e.g. tools.best(a, b) and tools.best([a, b, c]) both work. Never mix: don't append to a list and then also pass extra loose args in the same call.

block_optimize's block_size/max_gates bounds (block_size in {2,3,4}, 4<=max_gates<=200) are checked on EVERY call, not just the first; a later call that reuses hardcoded literals (e.g. block_size=4, max_gates=60) can still fail if those literals drift out of range when edited. Re-verify both bounds at each call site, not just once at the top.

Diff-style replies must contain the literal SEARCH block text copied exactly (verbatim whitespace/newlines, including trailing lines) from the parent program exactly once, and the SEARCH block must end on a complete statement (not mid-line, e.g. not cut off after a trailing comma like 'block_size=4, '). Truncated or re-indented SEARCH snippets cause 'unparseable response' rejection.

When editing via diff, copy the SEARCH block by selecting a short, unique, unmodified contiguous slice of the parent (e.g. one full if-block) rather than reconstructing the whole function from memory; retyping the entire body risks whitespace drift that makes SEARCH match 0 times.

Before returning/finishing an edit, re-read your own output: a program ending mid-line (e.g. 'top = tools.best(candidate') is truncated and will be rejected. If adding a new tail block, keep it short and complete, or trim an earlier low-value branch to make room.

If copying a block_optimize(...) call to a new call site, re-check its literal block_size/max_gates against {2,3,4} and [4,200] at that exact line; a previously-valid literal pasted into a new branch is still checked fresh and raises ToolError if out of range.

Growing a candidates list with tools.best(candidates) calls tends to truncate near the token limit (seen ending mid-line 'if tools'). Cap the chain: after ~5-6 if-blocks, stop adding new stages and just return tools.best(candidates); don't keep appending one more block 'just in case'.

block_optimize bound violations keep recurring even with literals in {2,3,4}/4-200: double-check the actual values at the call site you just wrote (not a remembered-safe pair) before submitting, especially when copy-pasting a block and changing one argument but not the other.

If a diff SEARCH block fails to match, don't retry by retyping the same remembered body a second time with small edits guessed at whitespace—re-fetch/quote the parent's literal text for that region verbatim, or switch to a full-file replacement instead of a diff.

When appending multiple tiered candidates (tr/blocked/blocked2/blocked3) to a growing `candidates` list, call tools.best(candidates) again after each append and reuse that running `top` as input to the next tool call, not the original `best`/`top` captured earlier—otherwise later blocks optimize a stale candidate and the extra tiers add runtime without improving the score.

Before submitting, scan every block_optimize call site in the final text for its two literal args (block_size, max_gates) independently—growing a program by appending new tiers often reuses a copy-pasted block whose block_size or max_gates was edited for one call but not a later duplicate, causing a ToolError that invalidates all circuits.

When a diff SEARCH fails once, do not resubmit a second diff guessing at the parent text again; switch that turn to a full-file replacement of the whole program body, since repeated diff retries on the same mismatch keep producing 'found 0 times' parse errors.

When a tail block gets cut by the response length limit (program ends mid-statement like 'blocked4 = t'), don't add another tier to an already-long program; truncation is a length problem, not a missing-feature problem. Finish the current tier cleanly and stop, or trim an earlier tier first.

Growing programs via repeated tiered if-blocks (tr/cs/blocked/blocked2/blocked3/blocked4...) tends to hit the output-length limit and truncate mid-line. Past ~5-6 tiers, prefer collapsing older tiers into a single tools.best(candidates) call rather than appending another near-duplicate if-block.

Before submitting a diff, verify the exact SEARCH text exists by locating it in the parent text you were given, not a paraphrase; if the parent was itself produced by truncation (ends mid-statement), a full-file replacement is safer than a diff against it.

Before submitting, count the time_left() thresholds used to gate tiered block_optimize/fold tiers you added in this turn: each new tier needs a strictly smaller threshold than the previous one and a complete body. If you can't finish writing and wiring a new tier within the remaining response length, don't start it—stop after the last complete tier instead of truncating mid-statement.

block_optimize requires max_gates in [4,200] and block_size in {2,3,4} for EVERY call site, not just the first. When copy-pasting a block_optimize line to add a new tier, explicitly re-check the new max_gates/block_size values against these bounds (e.g. max_gates must be >=4 even if you shrink block_size to 2) before submitting.

When growing a program with a diff, re-copy the SEARCH block from the literal parent text shown this turn, not from a previous turn's child you recall from memory—parents change between turns and a stale remembered body gives 'found 0 times'. If unsure the text matches exactly, use a full-file replacement instead.
